memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar along with the burnt offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord, a food offering presented to the Lord. After you take the breast of the ram for Aaron's ordination, wave it before the Lord as a wave offering, and it will be your share." - Exodus 29:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What the priests lifted up, God received. The offering is taken from their hands and burned on the altar, described again as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. Their giving did not vanish into empty air. It was accepted.

That phrase, "a pleasing aroma," appears repeatedly in these chapters, and it is worth pausing on. It means God was genuinely pleased. Not merely satisfied that a requirement had been met, but pleased — the way a parent is pleased by a child's gift, however modest. God is a receiver of offerings, not a distant collector of dues.

Paul uses this same language for ordinary Christian generosity, describing a gift sent to him as a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God (Phil 4:18). The kindness you show, the money you give, the time you offer, the service nobody notices — these rise to God as a pleasing aroma. Do not imagine your offerings go unnoticed. What you lift up, He receives, and He is genuinely pleased with what His children bring.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe God is genuinely pleased by what I offer Him?
What have I offered recently that I assumed went unnoticed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are a God who receives what Your children bring and is genuinely pleased. Thank You that nothing offered to You is wasted or unnoticed. Receive my offering today. Amen.
